theory.overview: Dynamic Programming (DP) solves complex problems by breaking them into simpler subproblems, storing results to avoid redundant computation. Key principles: optimal substructure (optimal solution contains optimal solutions to subproblems) and overlapping subproblems (same subproblems recur). DP trades space for time. This chapter covers DP fundamentals, memoization, tabulation, and classic 1D/2D DP problems.

sections.title: DP Principles
sections.content: Optimal substructure: can construct optimal solution from optimal solutions to subproblems. Overlapping subproblems: same subproblems solved multiple times (memoization helps). Memoization (top-down): recursive with caching. Tabulation (bottom-up): iterative table filling. State: parameters that uniquely identify subproblem. Transition: how to compute state from smaller states.

sections.title: Memoization vs Tabulation
sections.content: Memoization: recursive, cache results, intuitive, may have stack overflow. Tabulation: iterative, fill table, no recursion, often more efficient. Both achieve same time complexity. Memoization easier to implement for problems with natural recursion. Tabulation better for space optimization and avoiding stack limits.

sections.title: 1D DP
sections.content: Single-dimensional DP array. dp[i] represents solution for subproblem ending at or including i. Examples: climbing stairs (dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]), Fibonacci (dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]), house robber (dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i])). State space is linear.
examples: House robber: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i])

sections.title: 2D DP
sections.content: Two-dimensional DP table. dp[i][j] represents solution for subproblem involving first i rows and j columns (or similar). Examples: unique paths (dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]), edit distance, longest common subsequence. State space is grid.
examples: Edit distance: dp[i][j] based on operations
LCS: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if match else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])

sections.title: DP Pattern Recognition
sections.content: Look for: optimal substructure (can we break problem into smaller problems?), overlapping subproblems (same subproblems repeated?), choice at each step (which subproblem leads to optimal solution?). Common patterns: linear DP, interval DP, knapsack, LIS, LCS, tree DP. Practice pattern recognition to identify DP problems.

keyConcepts.name: Optimal Substructure
keyConcepts.description: Optimal solution can be constructed from optimal solutions to subproblems. Essential for DP validity.
keyConcepts.check: Can you solve smaller instances and combine?

keyConcepts.name: Overlapping Subproblems
keyConcepts.description: Same subproblems solved multiple times. Memoization caches results to avoid recomputation.

keyConcepts.name: State Definition
keyConcepts.description: Parameters that uniquely identify subproblem. Good state definition is key to DP solution.
keyConcepts.example: dp[i] = solution for first i elements

keyConcepts.name: Transition
keyConcepts.description: How to compute current state from previous states. The recurrence relation.

complexity.time: Depends on state space × transition cost
complexity.space: O(state space), can often be optimized

steps.title: Identify Subproblems
steps.description: Break problem into smaller subproblems. Identify what parameters define each subproblem.
steps.code: state = parameters that uniquely identify subproblem

steps.title: Define State
steps.description: Define dp array/table. dp[state] = answer for that subproblem.
steps.code: dp[i] = solution for subproblem with parameter i

steps.title: Define Transition
steps.description: Write recurrence relation. How to compute dp[i] from smaller states.

steps.title: Base Cases
steps.description: Define initial conditions. Smallest subproblems that can be solved directly.

steps.title: Fill DP Table
steps.description: Iterate through states in correct order (bottom-up) or use memoization (top-down).
steps.code: for i in range(2, n): dp[i] = transition(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]);

practiceProblems.title: Climbing Stairs
practiceProblems.description: Number of ways to climb n stairs (1 or 2 steps at a time).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Base: dp[0]=1, dp[1]=1. Can optimize to O(1) space.

practiceProblems.title: Fibonacci Number
practiceProblems.description: Compute nth Fibonacci number.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Base: dp[0]=0, dp[1]=1. O(1) space with two variables.

practiceProblems.title: House Robber
practiceProblems.description: Max money from robbing houses (can't rob adjacent houses).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]). Skip or take current house.

practiceProblems.title: House Robber II
practiceProblems.description: Houses arranged in circle (first and last adjacent).
practiceProblems.solution: Two cases: rob houses 0 to n-2, or 1 to n-1. Take max of both.
practiceProblems.hints: Two cases: exclude first or exclude last

practiceProblems.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
practiceProblems.description: Min cost to reach top of stairs (cost to step on stair i).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Return min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).

practiceProblems.title: Decode Ways
practiceProblems.description: Number of ways to decode string (A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if valid single digit) + dp[i-2] (if valid two digits).
practiceProblems.hints: Check single digit and two digit validity

practiceProblems.title: Unique Paths
practiceProblems.description: Number of unique paths from top-left to bottom-right in m×n grid (only right/down).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]. Can optimize to 1D.

practiceProblems.title: Unique Paths II
practiceProblems.description: Unique paths with obstacles in grid.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] = 0 if obstacle, else dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1].

practiceProblems.title: Coin Change
practiceProblems.description: Minimum coins to make amount (unlimited coins).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin] + 1) for each coin.

practiceProblems.title: Coin Change 2
practiceProblems.description: Number of ways to make amount (order doesn't matter).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] += dp[i-coin] for each coin (process coins one by one).
practiceProblems.hints: Process coins one by one to avoid counting permutations

practiceProblems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
practiceProblems.description: Length of longest strictly increasing subsequence.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) for j < i and nums[j] < nums[i]. Or patience sorting O(n log n).

practiceProblems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
practiceProblems.description: Length of LCS between two strings.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if match else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
practiceProblems.hints: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if match else max

practiceProblems.title: Edit Distance
practiceProblems.description: Minimum operations to convert word1 to word2 (insert, delete, replace).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] based on operations: replace, delete, insert.
practiceProblems.hints: dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j-1] + replace, dp[i-1][j] + delete, dp[i][j-1] + insert)

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Subarray
practiceProblems.description: Maximum sum of contiguous subarray.
practiceProblems.solution: Kadane's algorithm: dp[i] = max(nums[i], dp[i-1] + nums[i]).

practiceProblems.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
practiceProblems.description: Check if array can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum.
practiceProblems.solution: Subset sum DP. Check if sum/2 achievable.
practiceProblems.hints: Subset sum DP for target = sum/2

practiceProblems.title: Target Sum
practiceProblems.description: Number of ways to assign + and - to get target sum.
practiceProblems.solution: Subset sum variant. Find ways to get (target + sum(nums)) / 2.

practiceProblems.title: Combination Sum IV
practiceProblems.description: Number of combinations that add to target (order matters).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = sum(dp[i-num]) for all num. Order matters (permutations).

practiceProblems.title: Word Break
practiceProblems.description: Check if string can be segmented into dictionary words.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = true if s[0:i] can be segmented. dp[i] = any(dp[j] and s[j:i] in dict).
practiceProblems.hints: dp[i] = any(dp[j] and s[j:i] in dict)

practiceProblems.title: Word Break II
practiceProblems.description: Return all possible segmentations.
practiceProblems.solution: DP + backtracking. Memoize results for each position.

practiceProblems.title: Triangle
practiceProblems.description: Minimum path sum from top to bottom of triangle.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[j] = triangle[i][j] + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]). Bottom-up.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Path Sum
practiceProblems.description: Minimum path sum from top-left to bottom-right in grid.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

practiceProblems.title: Interleaving String
practiceProblems.description: Check if s3 is formed by interleaving s1 and s2.
practiceProblems.hints: dp[i][j] depends on previous states and character match

practiceProblems.title: Distinct Subsequences
practiceProblems.description: Number of distinct subsequences of s equal to t.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] if s[i-1]==t[j-1] else dp[i-1][j].

practiceProblems.title: Perfect Squares
practiceProblems.description: Least number of perfect square numbers that sum to n.
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = 1 + min(dp[i - j*j]) for all j*j ≤ i.

practiceProblems.title: Integer Break
practiceProblems.description: Maximum product of integers that sum to n (at least 2 positive integers).
practiceProblems.solution: dp[i] = max(max(j*(i-j), j*dp[i-j])) for j from 1 to i-1.
